Field.name: XStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Starting and ending X coordinate of region to cut out

Field.name: YStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Starting and ending Y coordinate of region to cut out

Field.name: ZStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Starting and ending Z coordinate of region to cut out

Field.name: XSize
Field.usage: Number of pixels to cut out in X, centered on the middle in X

Field.name: YSize
Field.usage: Number of pixels to cut out in Y, centered on the middle in Y

Field.name: ZSize
Field.usage: Number of slices to cut out in Z, centered on the middle in Z

Field.name: ZFindStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Scale to bytes, analyzing the given range of slices in Z
Field.manpage: Scale to bytes, or to another mode specified by \fB-mode\fR, by analyzing intensities from sections between the two given numbers, inclusive. Coordinates are treated as coming from a flipped volume only if the "-f" option is given. Slices are numbered from 1 regardless of whether the "-i" option is used. If the \fB-meansd\fR option is entered, scaling will be found by running Densmatch(1) and can be to any mode; if \fB-meansd\fR is not entered, scaling will be determined by running Findcontrast(1) and must be to bytes.

Field.name: XFindStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Starting and ending X coordinates to analyze for scaling to bytes
Field.manpage: Analyze the region between this starting and ending coordinate in X to determine the scaling invoked by either -\fB-sz\fR or \fB-meansd\fR. The default is to use 80% of the range in X.

Field.name: YFindStartAndEnd
Field.usage: Starting and ending Y coordinates to analyze for scaling to bytes
Field.manpage: Analyze the region between this starting and ending coordinate in Y to determine the scaling invoked by either -\fB-sz\fR or \fB-meansd\fR. The default is to use 80% of the range in Y.

Field.name: ContrastBlackWhite
Field.usage: Contrast levels for scaling and converting to bytes
Field.manpage: Scale to bytes, with relative intensities between the two entered numbers (representing black and white values on a scale of 0 to 255) stretched to occupy the full range of byte values.

Field.name: ScaleToMeanAndSD
Field.usage: Scale to the given mean and SD, convert to bytes by default
Field.manpage: Scale the image intensities to the given mean and standard deviation, then convert values to bytes (mode 0) unless the \fB-mode\fRoption is entered with a different mode.

Field.name: IntegerMinMax
Field.usage: Scale min and max to the given values, convert to integers by default
Field.manpage: Scale image intensities so that the minimum and maximum of the file become the given values of minimum and maximum, then convert values to integers (mode 1) unless the \fB-mode\fRoption is entered with a different mode. Newstack(1) is run with the \fB-scale\fR option and the entered values. This option has this name because it was originally used only to scale to integers.

Field.name: ModeToOutput
Field.usage: Storage mode of output file; 0 for byte, 1 or 6 for integer, 2 or 12 for float
Field.manpage: The storage mode of the output file; 0 for byte, 1 for 16-bit signed integer, 6 for 16-bit unsigned integer, 2 for 32-bit floating point, or 12 for 16-bit floats. This option can be used to modify the output mode for the \fB-mm\fR and \fB-meansd\fR options or when not applying any scaling at all, but cannot be used with the scaling to bytes invoked by the \fB-sz\fR or \fB-c\fR options. Mode 12 is allowed only if the output format is MRC.

Field.name: RotateX
Field.usage: Rotate volume by -90 degrees around X axis
Field.manpage: Rotate the output volume by -90 degrees around the X axis, by first creating a temporary trimmed volume with newstack then running "clip rotx" on this volume to create the final output file. The slices will look the same as with the "-yz" option but rotating instead of flipping will preserve the handedness of structures.

Field.name: FlipYZ
Field.usage: Exchange (flip) Y and Z in output volume
Field.manpage: Flip Y and Z in the output volume by first creating a temporary trimmed volume with newstack then running "clip flipyz" on this volume to create the final output file. Do not use this option unless you intend to invert handedness.

Field.name: FormatOfOutputFile
Field.usage: Type of output file: MRC, TIF or TIFF, HDF (or lower case)
Field.manpage: Set output file format to MRC, TIFF, or HDF by entering MRC, TIF, TIFF, HDF, or any lower case form of these. This entry overrides a default format set with the environment variable IMOD_OUTPUT_FORMAT.

Field.name: IndexCoordinates
Field.usage: Treat as index coordinates (numbered from 0) rather than as 3dmod coordinates (numbered from 1, the default)
Field.manpage: Interpret "-x", "-y", "-z", "-sx", and "-sy" entries as index coordinates numbered from 0, rather than as 3dmod coordinates numbered from 1.

Field.name: FlippedCoordinates
Field.usage: Treat coordinates as coming from a volume viewed with flipping in 3dmod
Field.manpage: Interpret "-y", "-z", "-ny", "-nz", "-sy", and "-sz" entries as referring to a volume viewed in flipped orientation in 3dmod, with Y and Z sizes swapped. This option allows you to enter the coordinates as they appear in 3dmod when the volume is loaded with flipping (the -Y option). The program assumes that flipping occurred by rotating around the X axis, unless the "-old" option is given.

Field.name: OldFlippedCoordinates
Field.usage: Some or all Z coordinates are based on flipping with Y and Z axes swapped
Field.manpage: This option indicates that Z coordinates were obtained by loading the volume with the -Y option into a version of 3dmod prior to 4.6.18, where flipping was done by exchanging the Y and Y axes instead of rotating around X. Enter the sum of 1 if the "-z" entry is based on such flipping and 2 if the "-sz" entry is based on such flipping.

Field.name: KeepOrigin
Field.usage: Keep origin the same in output from Newstack (legacy)
Field.manpage: Keep the origin the same in the output from Newstack(1) instead of passing it the -origin option to adjust the origin for the location of the subvolume being created. This option can be used to reproduce a volume created with earlier versions of IMOD.

Field.name: PID
Field.usage: Print process ID
